evidence.quote: We first describe an unsupervised approach, which takes an input sentence and predicts itself in a contrastive objective, with only standard dropout used as noise.
We find that dropout acts as minimal data augmentation and removing it leads to a representation collapse.

More recently, remarkable advancements have been achieved by contrastive learning (CL) on sentence embeddings (Gao et al., 2021), which cleverly makes use of dropout randomness (Bouthillier et al., 2015) to construct positive pairs in an unsupervised way.
In this paper, we improve the sentence embedding models from two perspectives: dropout noise and feature corruption.
We find that modest dropout noise in the positive pairs is beneficial to the model performance whereas dropout noise in negative pairs is harmful.
Based on these findings, we propose a simple yet effective strategy, offdropout, which turns off the dropout randomness in negative pairs to further improve the performance.
As a result, by combining the proposed offdropout and DCL, we have advanced the SimCSE baseline by 1.9 points.
